reuse.why: Puts the rule in the existing getScheduledAmount and reuses the matcher's own getApproxNumberThreshold for the tolerance instead of re-deriving 7.5%.

duplication.why: No logic is duplicated; call sites only pass the operator they already have.

placement.why: The expected-amount rule stays in shared/schedules.ts, the shared definition used by server and client.

scope.why: Focused on the approximate rule; inserting op before the inverse parameter forced test rewrites, and display-only call sites (table/list amount cells) now also show the worst-case value, which goes slightly beyond planning.

maintainability.why: One definition with one more input is easy to own, though an optional op defaulting to null means a future caller that forgets it silently gets the exact amount for approximate schedules.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every planning/expectation path goes through getScheduledAmount; the editor's operator-switch conversions in useScheduleEdit intentionally keep the raw amount.

one_place.where: getScheduledAmount in packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts, with every expected-amount call site (server posting, preview, forecast, templates, API, balance, schedule lists) passing the operator.
